source.sourceQuote: Any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid.

questions.question: Where does the manual say dirt and gravel particularly collect?
choices: Along the sides of the road, especially on curves and ramps leading to and from highways
In the left tire track of the lane
At the crown in the centre of the road
On bridge decks and overpasses
questions.explanation: The manual says dirt and gravel collect along the sides of the road, especially on curves and ramps leading to and from highways, and tells you to be aware of what is on the edge of the road, particularly when making sharp turns and getting on or off freeways at high speeds.
choiceExplanations: The tire tracks are where traction is usually best in the wet, not where gravel gathers.
The centre of the lane collects oil and debris from cars, not road-edge gravel.
Bridges and overpasses are named for ice, not for accumulated gravel.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Wet pavement, particularly just after it starts to rain and before surface oil washes to the side of the road.

questions.question: How will you usually first notice a tire going flat?
choices: The motorcycle starts handling differently
You hear the tire deflate
The brake lever travel increases
The engine note changes
questions.explanation: The manual says you will seldom hear a tire go flat, and that if the motorcycle starts handling differently, it may be a tire failure. A front tire going down makes the steering feel heavy; a rear one makes the back of the motorcycle jerk or sway from side to side.
choiceExplanations: The manual says you will seldom hear a tire go flat; the warning is a change in handling.
Brake lever travel relates to the hydraulic system, not to tire pressure.
A change in engine sound is the first sign of engine seizure, a different failure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If the motorcycle starts handling differently, it may be a tire failure.

questions.question: A tire goes flat while you are riding. What is the first thing to do?
choices: Hold the handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle and keep a straight course
Apply both brakes firmly to stop as soon as possible
Swerve to the shoulder immediately
Downshift rapidly to use engine braking
questions.explanation: The manual says that if either tire goes flat while riding, hold the handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle and keep a straight course. If braking is required, gradually apply the brake of the tire that is not flat, if you are sure which one it is; when the motorcycle slows, edge to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch and stop.
choiceExplanations: Braking both wheels on a flat tire risks losing control of the wheel that has no air in it.
A sudden change of direction on a failing tire is exactly the input to avoid.
Rapid downshifting sends a sudden power change to a wheel that may be the flat one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Hold handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep a straight course.

questions.question: If you must brake with a flat tire and you are sure which tire it is, what does the manual say?
choices: Gradually apply the brake of the tire that is not flat
Use both brakes together as normal
Use only the front brake, as it has the most power
Use only the rear brake, as it is less likely to lock
questions.explanation: The manual's instruction is conditional and specific: if braking is required, gradually apply the brake of the tire that isn't flat, if you are sure which one it is. If you are not sure, the safer course is to let the motorcycle slow with the throttle closed.
choiceExplanations: Both brakes together applies braking force to the failed tire as well as the good one.
The front brake is the wrong choice if the front tire is the one that has gone down.
Rear-only braking is wrong when the rear is the flat tire.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Hold handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep a straight course.

questions.question: Your throttle sticks open. What does the manual say to try first?
choices: Twist the throttle back and forth several times
Operate the engine cut-off switch straight away
Squeeze the clutch and brake hard
Switch off the ignition key
questions.explanation: The manual says that if the situation allows, twist the throttle back and forth several times — if the throttle cable is stuck, this may free it. Only if the throttle stays stuck do you move to the cut-off switch.
choiceExplanations: The cut-off switch is the second step, used if twisting does not free the cable.
Braking against an open throttle is a fight you do not need to have if the cable frees.
The manual names the engine cut-off switch, not the ignition key, as the control to use.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If the situation allows, twist the throttle back and forth several times.

questions.question: Twisting has not freed a stuck throttle. What does the manual say to do?
choices: Operate the engine cut-off switch and squeeze the clutch lever at the same time
Brake hard and hold the motorcycle against the engine
Shift up through the gears to reduce engine speed
Turn off the fuel valve and wait for the engine to run dry
questions.explanation: The manual says that if the throttle stays stuck, immediately operate the engine cut-off switch and squeeze the clutch lever at the same time. This removes power from the rear wheel, although engine sound may not immediately decline. Then move to a safe area and stop.
choiceExplanations: Braking against an open throttle wastes distance and may still not stop the motorcycle.
Upshifting keeps the engine driving the rear wheel, just at a different ratio.
Waiting for a fuel line to empty takes far too long to be an emergency response.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If the throttle stays stuck, immediately operate the engine cut-off switch and squeeze the clutch lever at the same time.

questions.question: What is a 'wobble'?
choices: The front wheel and handlebars suddenly shaking from side to side at any speed
The rear wheel sliding out under braking
The motorcycle weaving on a bridge grating
A vibration that only occurs above 60 mph
questions.explanation: The manual defines a wobble as occurring when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly start to shake from side to side at any speed. That 'at any speed' is deliberate — riders often assume it is a high-speed-only problem.
choiceExplanations: A sliding rear wheel is a rear-wheel skid, a braking problem with different rules.
Weaving on a grating comes from the road surface and is generally not hazardous.
The manual says a wobble can occur at any speed, not only at high speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: A “wobble” occurs when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly start to shake from side to side at any speed.

questions.question: Most wobbles can be traced to what?
choices: Improper loading, unsuitable accessories or incorrect tire pressure
Worn brake pads or low brake fluid
Riding at low speed in too high a gear
Uneven road camber
questions.explanation: The manual says most wobbles can be traced to improper loading, unsuitable accessories or incorrect tire pressure. Its first fixes are to lighten or reposition a heavy load, centre the weight lower and farther forward, and check tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks and dampers against the settings for the weight carried.
choiceExplanations: Brake wear affects stopping, not the side-to-side shake of the front end.
Gear selection does not cause a front-end wobble.
Road camber is not identified as a cause of wobble in the manual.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Most wobbles can be traced to improper loading, unsuitable accessories or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: The front end of your motorcycle begins shaking violently from side to side. What is the correct response?
choices: Hold the handlebars firmly and roll off the throttle gradually
Open the throttle to power through the shake
Apply the brakes progressively until the shake stops
Pull in the clutch and coast with a light, relaxed grip
questions.explanation: The manual's response is to grip the handlebars firmly but not fight the wobble, close the throttle gradually to slow down, move your weight as far forward and down as possible, and pull off the road as soon as you can to fix the problem. It expressly rules out both accelerating and braking.
choiceExplanations: The manual says trying to accelerate out of a wobble will only make the motorcycle more unstable.
The manual says not to apply the brakes, because braking could make the wobble worse.
A light grip is wrong: the manual asks you to grip firmly, while not fighting the wobble.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Grip the handlebars firmly, but don't fight the wobble.

questions.question: Which action does the manual specifically warn against during a wobble?
choices: Applying the brakes
Closing the throttle gradually
Gripping the handlebars firmly
Moving your weight forward and down
questions.explanation: The manual says to close the throttle gradually to slow down and adds: do not apply the brakes, braking could make the wobble worse. It separately rules out trying to accelerate out of a wobble, which only makes the motorcycle more unstable.
choiceExplanations: This is the correct response — it slows the motorcycle without a sudden input.
This is correct — grip firmly, but do not fight the wobble.
This is correct — the manual asks for weight as far forward and down as possible.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Close the throttle gradually to slow down. Do not apply the brakes; braking could make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What will you notice if the drive chain or belt breaks while riding?
choices: An instant loss of power to the rear wheel
The engine stopping immediately
The front brake losing pressure
The handlebars shaking from side to side
questions.explanation: The manual says that if the chain or belt breaks, you will notice an instant loss of power to the rear wheel, and to close the throttle and brake to a stop in a safe area. The greater danger is a chain or belt that slips or breaks and locks the rear wheel, causing a skid.
choiceExplanations: The engine keeps running; what it loses is its connection to the rear wheel.
The brakes are hydraulically or mechanically independent of the drive train.
A side-to-side shake is a wobble, which has different causes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If the chain or belt breaks, you'll notice an instant loss of power to the rear wheel.

questions.question: What usually causes an engine to lock or freeze?
choices: It is low on oil
The fuel valve has been left closed
The chain has been over-tightened
The clutch cable has snapped
questions.explanation: The manual says that when the engine locks or freezes it is usually low on oil, so the moving parts cannot move smoothly against each other and the engine overheats. The first sign may be a loss of engine power or a change in the engine's sound.
choiceExplanations: A closed fuel valve stalls the engine once the lines empty; it does not seize it.
Chain tension affects the drive train, not the engine's internal lubrication.
A broken clutch cable prevents disengagement but does not seize the engine.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: When the engine “locks” or “freezes” it is usually low on oil.

questions.question: The engine loses power and its sound changes. What does the manual tell you to do?
choices: Squeeze the clutch lever to disengage the engine from the rear wheel, then pull off and stop
Brake hard immediately to stop before the engine fails
Accelerate to a service station before it seizes
Switch to reserve fuel and continue
questions.explanation: The manual says to squeeze the clutch lever to disengage the engine from the rear wheel, pull off the road and stop, then check the oil. When an engine seizes the effect is the same as a locked rear wheel, so disengaging it first is what prevents the skid.
choiceExplanations: Hard braking does nothing about the risk that a seizing engine locks the rear wheel.
Riding on is how a warning becomes a seizure, which has the same effect as a locked rear wheel.
Fuel supply is unrelated to a seizure caused by low oil.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Squeeze the clutch lever to disengage the engine from the rear wheel.

questions.question: A small animal runs into your path while you are riding in traffic. What does the manual advise?
choices: Remain in your lane — hitting something small is less dangerous than hitting a car
Swerve into the next lane to miss it
Brake as hard as possible regardless of the traffic behind
Sound your horn and maintain speed and position
questions.explanation: The manual says to do everything you safely can to avoid hitting an animal, but if you are in traffic, remain in your lane, because hitting something small is less dangerous to you than hitting something big — like a car.
choiceExplanations: Swerving into another lane in traffic trades a small impact for a collision with a vehicle.
Maximum braking in traffic invites being struck from behind for a minor hazard.
The horn is a useful tool but is not the manual's instruction for an animal in traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If you are in traffic, however, remain in your lane.

questions.question: A dog runs out and starts chasing alongside you. What sequence does the manual give?
choices: Downshift, approach it slowly, then accelerate away as you reach it
Accelerate hard straight away to outrun it
Kick out at the dog so it backs off
Come to a halt and wait for it to lose interest
questions.explanation: The manual says that if you are being chased, downshift and approach the animal slowly, and as you approach it, accelerate and leave the animal behind. It adds: don't kick at the animal — keep control of your motorcycle and look to where you want to go.
choiceExplanations: Accelerating comes only as you reach the animal, after approaching it slowly.
The manual says not to kick at the animal — it costs you control of the motorcycle.
Stopping puts you at a standstill beside an agitated animal with no escape.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: approach it, accelerate and leave the animal behind. Don't kick at the animal.

questions.question: A deer steps into the road ahead of you. What does the manual advise?
choices: Brake and prepare to stop, because larger animals are unpredictable
Maintain speed and swerve around it
Accelerate past before it moves again
Sound the horn and hold your lane position
questions.explanation: The manual treats large animals differently from small ones: for larger animals such as deer, elk and cattle, brake and prepare to stop, because they are unpredictable. A deer is not a small impact you ride through.
choiceExplanations: Swerving at speed around an unpredictable animal is how the animal ends up in your new path.
Accelerating removes the time you need if the animal moves the way you did not expect.
The horn is not the manual's answer for large animals; braking and preparing to stop is.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: For larger animals (deer, elk, cattle) brake and prepare to stop - they are unpredictable.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches the animal to the manual's advice?
choices: Small animal in traffic: stay in your lane. Deer: brake and prepare to stop
Small animal in traffic: swerve. Deer: maintain speed
Small animal in traffic: brake hard. Deer: swerve around it
Both: swerve into the adjacent lane
questions.explanation: The manual gives two different answers. For small animals in traffic, remain in your lane, since hitting something small is less dangerous than hitting a car. For larger animals — deer, elk, cattle — brake and prepare to stop, because they are unpredictable.
choiceExplanations: Swerving in traffic for a small animal is precisely what the manual rules out.
Hard braking is the response for large animals, not small ones in traffic.
Leaving your lane in traffic is the one thing the manual tells you not to do.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Hitting something small is less dangerous to you than hitting something big - like a car.

questions.question: An insect strikes your faceshield and smears your view. What does the manual say to do?
choices: Keep your eyes on the road and your hands on the handlebars, then pull off when safe
Raise the shield immediately to clear your view
Wipe the shield with your glove while riding
Brake hard and stop in the traffic lane
questions.explanation: The manual says that whatever happens, keep your eyes on the road and your hands on the handlebars, and when safe, pull off the road and repair the damage. The strike itself is rarely the danger; taking your hands or eyes away from the task is.
choiceExplanations: Raising a shield at speed exposes your eyes to the very debris that caused the problem.
Taking a hand off the handlebars to wipe the shield is the loss of control the manual warns about.
Stopping in a live traffic lane creates a far greater hazard than a smeared shield.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Whatever happens, keep your eyes on the road and your hands on the handlebars.

questions.question: Before riding onto the roadside to stop, what should you check?
choices: That the surface of the roadside is firm enough to ride on
That you are within a mile of a service station
That the shoulder is wide enough to turn around on
That there are no vehicles parked further along
questions.explanation: The manual's first step for getting off the road is to check the roadside: make sure the surface is firm enough to ride on. If it is soft grass, loose sand, or you are simply not sure about it, slow way down before you turn onto it.
choiceExplanations: Distance to services is not part of the manual's four-step check.
Turning space is not what the manual names; surface firmness is.
Other parked vehicles matter for where you stop, but the first check is the surface.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Make sure the surface of the roadside is firm enough to ride on.

questions.question: Why does the manual say to get as far off the road as you can when you stop?
choices: A motorcycle by the roadside is hard to spot, and someone else may pull off in the same place
It is a legal requirement on all highways
It keeps the exhaust away from dry grass
It makes the side stand easier to set
questions.explanation: The manual says to get as far off the road as you can, because it can be very hard to spot a motorcycle by the side of the road and you do not want someone else pulling off at the same place you are. It also reminds you to park carefully, since loose and sloped shoulders make setting the side or centre stand difficult.
choiceExplanations: The manual gives a visibility and collision reason, not a legal one.
Fire risk is not among the manual's reasons for pulling well clear.
Loose and sloped shoulders actually make setting the stand harder, which is a separate caution.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Get as far off the road as you can.

questions.question: What does the manual say about signalling before you leave the road?
choices: Give a clear signal that you will be slowing down and changing direction
No signal is needed if you are leaving the road rather than turning
Use the horn instead of a signal
Signal only if another vehicle is directly behind you
questions.explanation: The manual says drivers behind might not expect you to slow down, so give a clear signal that you will be slowing down and changing direction, and check your mirror and make a head check before you take any action.
choiceExplanations: Leaving the road is a change of speed and direction, which is exactly what signals communicate.
The horn announces presence; it does not tell anyone what you are about to do.
The manual asks for a clear signal regardless, and for a mirror check and head check as well.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Give a clear signal that you will be slowing down and changing direction.

questions.question: Who does the manual say should attempt to carry passengers or large loads?
choices: Only experienced riders
Any licensed rider
Any rider with a full-face helmet
Any rider whose motorcycle is over 500cc
questions.explanation: The manual says the extra weight of a passenger or cargo will affect the way your motorcycle handles, requiring extra practice, preparation and caution, and for this reason only experienced riders should attempt to carry passengers or large loads.
choiceExplanations: A licence is a minimum, not the standard the manual sets for carrying a passenger.
Helmet type is a gear question and has nothing to do with carrying a passenger.
Engine size is not the criterion the manual uses.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: only experienced riders should attempt to carry passengers or large loads

questions.question: Which of these does the manual require before carrying a passenger?
choices: Passenger footrests
A backrest
A top box
A passenger seat belt
questions.explanation: The manual says to be sure your motorcycle is equipped with passenger footrests, that it has a proper seat large enough to hold both of you without crowding, and that there is a strap or solid handholds for your passenger to hold onto.
choiceExplanations: A backrest is not among the manual's requirements for carrying a passenger.
A top box is luggage, not passenger equipment.
The manual calls for a strap or solid handholds, not a seat belt.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: Be sure your motorcycle is equipped with passenger footrests.

questions.question: What level of protective gear should a passenger wear?
choices: The same level of personal protective gear as the rider
A helmet only
Whatever they find comfortable
A helmet and gloves, since they are not operating the controls
questions.explanation: The manual says to be sure your passenger is properly attired, wearing the same level of personal protective gear as you. A passenger hits the road at the same speed the rider does.
choiceExplanations: A helmet alone leaves the passenger without the clothing and boot protection the rider has.
Comfort is not the standard; the manual sets the rider's own gear level as the benchmark.
Not operating the controls does not reduce a passenger's exposure in a crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: Be sure your passenger is properly attired, wearing the same level of personal protective gear as you.

questions.question: What should a passenger do in turns and curves?
choices: Stay directly behind you and lean with you
Lean the opposite way to balance the motorcycle
Sit upright and not lean at all
Lean further than the rider to help the motorcycle turn
questions.explanation: The manual instructs the passenger to stay directly behind you and lean with you through turns and curves, adding that it helps for the passenger to look over the rider's shoulder in the direction of the turn. Passengers should also avoid unnecessary conversation and sudden moves.
choiceExplanations: Counter-leaning fights the lean the motorcycle needs to turn.
Staying rigidly upright puts the passenger's weight out of line with the motorcycle's lean.
Over-leaning is an unpredictable input that upsets the motorcycle's stability.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: Stay directly behind you and lean with you through turns and curves.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on the motorcycle?
choices: Only after the engine is started and the transmission is in neutral
Before the rider starts the engine
Once the motorcycle is already moving slowly
Only when the motorcycle is on its centre stand
questions.explanation: The manual tells you to instruct your passenger to get on the motorcycle only after you have started the engine and have the transmission in neutral, and that as the passenger mounts you keep both your feet on the ground and the front brake applied.
choiceExplanations: The manual specifies mounting after the engine is running and the bike is in neutral.
Mounting a moving motorcycle is dangerous and is nowhere suggested.
The manual does not require the centre stand; it requires the rider's feet down and front brake applied.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: Get on the motorcycle only after you have started the engine and have the transmission in neutral.

questions.question: Why must a passenger keep both feet on the footrests even when the motorcycle is stopped?
choices: Firm footing prevents the passenger falling off and pulling you off
It keeps their weight off the seat springs
It stops them touching the exhaust
It is required for the motorcycle to stay in neutral
questions.explanation: The manual's reason is direct: keep both feet firmly on the footrests, even when stopped, because firm footing will prevent your passenger from falling off and pulling you off. A passenger who plants a foot at a stop can unbalance the motorcycle and both of you.
choiceExplanations: Seat springs are not a concern the manual raises.
Keeping legs away from the muffler is separate advice; footrest use is about stability.
Neutral is a transmission state, unaffected by where a passenger's feet are.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: Keep both feet firmly on the footrests, even when stopped.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger be placed?
choices: Immediately behind the rider
In front of the rider, where they can be watched
Behind any adult passenger
On the tank, with a purpose-made seat
questions.explanation: The manual says children should be placed immediately behind the rider, and explains why: a child sitting in front of the rider will not be able to properly balance him or herself and may interfere with the rider's control of the motorcycle.
choiceExplanations: The manual says a child in front cannot balance properly and may interfere with your control.
The manual places children immediately behind the rider, not further back.
No tank seating arrangement is described or endorsed in the manual.

questions.question: Which statement about carrying a child is NOT correct?
choices: A child may sit in front of the rider if they are small enough to hold on
A child should be placed immediately behind the rider
A child must be able to reach the passenger footrests
A child needs the same level of protective gear as the rider
questions.explanation: The manual rules this out directly: a child sitting in front of the rider will not be able to properly balance him or herself and may interfere with the rider's control of the motorcycle. Size does not change that.
choiceExplanations: This is correct — the manual places children immediately behind the rider.
This is correct — the manual says to ensure your passenger can reach the passenger footrests.
This is correct — every passenger wears the same level of gear as the rider.

questions.question: How does a heavier passenger change the motorcycle's behaviour?
choices: It takes longer to speed up, slow down or turn
It shortens stopping distance because of the extra weight on the tires
It makes the steering lighter
It has no measurable effect below highway speeds
questions.explanation: The manual says your motorcycle will respond differently with a passenger, and the heavier your passenger, the longer it may take to speed up, slow down, or turn. That is why you ride a little slower, start slowing earlier, and wait for larger gaps to cross, enter or merge.
choiceExplanations: Extra weight lengthens stopping distance; the manual says to start slowing earlier.
Extra weight over the rear lightens the front, but the manual's point is slower response overall.
The manual gives no speed threshold below which a passenger stops mattering.

questions.question: You are carrying a passenger and need to pull out across a busy junction. What does the manual advise?
choices: Wait for a larger gap than you would need riding alone
Use the same gap you would alone, but accelerate harder
Use a smaller gap, since two riders are easier for drivers to see
Have the passenger dismount and cross on foot
questions.explanation: The manual's instruction for riding with a passenger includes waiting for larger gaps to cross, enter, or merge in traffic, because the extra weight means it takes longer to speed up. The gap that was adequate solo is not adequate two up.
choiceExplanations: Accelerating harder does not overcome the slower response a loaded motorcycle has.
Being more visible does not make the motorcycle accelerate faster into a small gap.
Nothing in the manual suggests dismounting passengers at junctions.

questions.question: Where should cargo be placed on a motorcycle?
choices: Over, or in front of, the rear axle
Behind the rear axle, on a rack
As high as possible to keep it clear of the wheel
Split evenly between the tank and the tail
questions.explanation: The manual says to try to place the load over, or in front of, the rear axle, because mounting loads behind the rear axle can affect how the motorcycle turns and brakes, and can also cause a wobble.
choiceExplanations: Mounting loads behind the rear axle affects how the motorcycle turns and brakes and can cause a wobble.
A high load raises the centre of gravity and can upset the motorcycle's balance.
The manual gives a single placement rule, not a front-and-back split.

questions.question: Why does the manual say to secure loads low or in saddlebags?
choices: Attaching a load higher raises the centre of gravity and can upset the motorcycle's balance
A high load catches more wind and slows the motorcycle
Low loads are easier to reach while riding
Saddlebags are the only legal way to carry cargo
questions.explanation: The manual says to secure loads low, or put them in saddlebags, because attaching a load higher raises the motorcycle's centre of gravity and can upset its balance. Weight high and far back is the combination that produces wobble.
choiceExplanations: Wind resistance is not the reason the manual gives.
Reaching cargo while riding is not something the manual encourages.
The manual describes several luggage options; saddlebags are not a legal requirement.

questions.question: What does the manual recommend for fastening a load?
choices: Elastic cords such as bungee cords or nets, with more than one attachment point per side
Rope tied with a secure knot
Adhesive tape around the load and the seat
The passenger holding the load in place
questions.explanation: The manual says to fasten the load securely with elastic cords — bungee cords or nets — and recommends elastic cords with more than one attachment point per side. It warns that rope can stretch and knots can come loose, permitting the load to shift or fall.
choiceExplanations: The manual warns that rope can stretch and knots can come loose, letting the load shift or fall.
Tape is nowhere mentioned as a method of securing a load.
A passenger's job is to hold onto the motorcycle, not to hold cargo.

questions.question: What can happen if a load is loose or a saddlebag is overloaded?
choices: It can catch in the wheel or chain, lock the rear wheel and cause a skid
It will only affect fuel consumption
It will trigger the anti-lock braking system
It will cause the headlight beam to drop
questions.explanation: The manual warns that overloading may cause saddlebags to catch in the wheel or chain, locking the rear wheel and causing the motorcycle to skid, and that a loose load could catch in the wheel or chain and lock it up the same way. It tells you to stop and check the load often.
choiceExplanations: The manual identifies a control hazard, not an economy one.
ABS responds to wheel lock under braking, not to luggage.
Beam height is affected by load and is re-aimed before the ride, but that is not this hazard.

questions.question: You pack saddlebags with very different weights on each side. What does the manual say will happen?
choices: The motorcycle will pull to one side
The rear suspension will fail
The motorcycle will steer more precisely
The brake light will stay on
questions.explanation: The manual says that if you use saddlebags, load each with about the same weight, because an uneven load can cause the motorcycle to pull to one side. It is the same family of problem as improper loading causing a wobble.
choiceExplanations: Suspension failure is not what the manual attributes to uneven loading.
Uneven loading degrades handling rather than improving it.
Electrical behaviour is unrelated to how saddlebags are packed.

questions.question: Who should the lead rider and sweep rider be?
choices: The most experienced riders of the group
The two riders with the largest motorcycles
Whoever knows the route
The newest riders, so they are watched from both ends
questions.explanation: The manual says to choose a lead rider and a sweep rider, and that these should be the most experienced riders of the group. The lead rider looks ahead for changes in road, traffic or weather and signals early; the sweep rider is last and sets the pace.
choiceExplanations: Motorcycle size is not a criterion the manual uses for group roles.
The whole group should know the route, agreed at the rider's meeting.
Inexperienced riders go just behind the leader, not into the lead or sweep roles.

questions.question: Why does the manual say to hold a rider's meeting before a group ride?
choices: So everyone knows the route and a separated rider need not hurry to catch up
So the group can agree a speed above the limit for open sections
So riders can be assigned to ride in pairs
So the newest rider can lead and set a safe pace
questions.explanation: The manual says to hold a rider's meeting to discuss the route, length of riding segments, rest stops and locations for fuel, meals and lodging, and to make sure everyone knows the route, so that if someone becomes separated they will not have to hurry to keep from getting lost or making the wrong turn.
choiceExplanations: Nothing in the manual contemplates agreeing to exceed speed limits.
The manual says never to ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane.
The lead role goes to an experienced rider; the sweep rider sets the pace.

questions.question: Which position in the group does the manual assign to its least experienced riders?
choices: Immediately behind the lead rider
At the very back of the group
At the front, setting the group's pace
Paired alongside a more experienced rider
questions.explanation: The manual says to place inexperienced riders just behind the leader, which ensures they will not have to chase after the group and lets the more experienced riders watch them from the back.
choiceExplanations: The back is the sweep rider's position, and the sweep should be one of the most experienced.
Leading requires the experience to read the road and signal changes early for the group.
Riding beside another rider in the same lane is expressly ruled out.

questions.question: What does the sweep rider do?
choices: Rides last and sets the pace for the group
Rides first and chooses the route
Rides alongside the leader to share navigation
Rides at the mid-point to relay signals
questions.explanation: The manual says the sweep rider is the last rider in the group, and sets the pace for the group. Both the lead and the sweep should be among the most experienced riders present.
choiceExplanations: The lead rider goes first and looks ahead for changes in road, traffic and weather.
Riding alongside another rider in the same lane is against the manual's rules.
No mid-group relay role is described in the manual.

questions.question: What does the manual name as the most important rules for group riding?
choices: No competition, no passing of other riders and no tailgating
Ride two abreast, keep formation, and never signal
Keep the group under five riders and always use hand signals
Ride single file at all times and never stop
questions.explanation: The manual states that the most important rules for group riding are: no competition, no passing of other riders and no tailgating. It adds that if a rider insists on riding faster than the group, let them go ahead to an agreed meeting point.
choiceExplanations: Riding two abreast in a lane is expressly forbidden, and signals are always used.
No group size limit appears, and hand signals supplement rather than replace the rules.
Staggered formation is the normal arrangement; single file is used in specific situations.

questions.question: Why does the manual say never to ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane?
choices: There is no place to go if you have to avoid a car or a hazard
It makes the group harder for drivers to see
It is illegal in every state
The two motorcycles' wind blasts interfere with each other
questions.explanation: The manual says never to ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane, because there is no place to go if you have to manoeuvre to avoid a car or hazard in the roadway. It adds that if you want to talk, wait until you are both stopped.
choiceExplanations: A close group is actually easier to see; the problem is the absence of an escape path.
The manual gives a safety reason, not a legal one.
Aerodynamic interference is not a hazard the manual raises.

questions.question: In a staggered formation, where does the second rider ride?
choices: At least one second back, in the right side of the lane
At least two seconds back, in the right side of the lane
Directly beside the leader
At least one second back, in the left side of the lane
questions.explanation: The manual describes the formation precisely: the group leader rides in the left side of the lane, and the second rider stays at least one second back and rides in the right side of the lane. The third maintains the left position of the lane, at least two seconds behind the first rider.
choiceExplanations: Two seconds is the spacing for the third rider relative to the leader.
Riding beside another rider in the same lane is expressly forbidden.
The leader holds the left side; the second rider takes the right side.

questions.question: How far behind the leader should the third rider in a staggered formation be?
choices: At least two seconds
At least one second
At least four seconds
Directly behind, with no set gap
questions.explanation: The manual says the third rider maintains the left position of the lane, at least two seconds behind the first rider, and that the fourth keeps at least a two-second distance from the second rider on the right, and so on. The pattern keeps ranks close while preserving each rider's own cushion.
choiceExplanations: One second is the second rider's spacing behind the leader.
Four seconds is not a formation figure; it is the SEE strategy's immediate path.
The manual gives specific spacing rather than leaving it to judgement.

questions.question: What does the manual say about intersections when riding in a group?
choices: They present the highest risk for motorcyclists in a group
They are safer in a group because the group is more visible
They should always be crossed two abreast to shorten the group
They require the group to split into pairs
questions.explanation: The manual states that intersections present the highest risk for motorcyclists in a group. When making a left turn with a turn arrow, tighten the formation to get as many riders through as possible — but make the turn single file, not side by side.
choiceExplanations: Visibility helps, but the manual identifies intersections as the group's highest-risk point.
The manual says to make turns single file and not to ride side by side.
Riders never pair up in a lane, at intersections or anywhere else.

questions.question: The light changes and only half the group gets through the junction. What does the manual advise?
choices: Those through should stop at a safe point ahead and wait
The riders left behind should follow through the red light to keep the group together
The group should split permanently and meet at the destination
The lead rider should return to the junction
questions.explanation: The manual says that if not all riders get through the light, stop at a safe point ahead and wait. It gives the reason directly: this will prevent riders from feeling pressured to speed up or run a red light.
choiceExplanations: Running a red light is exactly the pressure the manual's advice exists to remove.
Splitting up is unnecessary when a short wait reunites the group safely.
Turning back into the junction adds risk rather than removing it.

questions.question: On a two-lane highway, how should a staggered group pass slower traffic?
choices: One rider at a time, each judging oncoming traffic for themselves
As a single unit, following the leader through the gap
In pairs, to halve the time spent in the opposing lane
Only when the sweep rider signals that the way is clear
questions.explanation: The manual says that on a two-lane highway, riders in a staggered formation should pass one at a time. Each rider must have a clear view of oncoming traffic, because just because the lead rider passed does not mean conditions have not changed.
choiceExplanations: Passing as a unit is what the manual permits on a freeway or interstate, not on a two-lane road.
Riding in pairs is against the manual's rule on never riding alongside another rider.
The sweep rider sets the pace but does not clear passes for the riders ahead.

questions.question: After the lead rider completes a pass on a two-lane road, where should they go?
choices: Return to the left position and continue at passing speed to open room for the next rider
Move to the right side of the lane immediately
Slow to the original group speed at once
Pull onto the shoulder and wait for the group
questions.explanation: The manual says the lead rider should return to the left position and continue at passing speed to open room for the next rider. It explicitly rejects moving to the right side after passing, because it might encourage the second rider to pass and cut back in before there is enough space cushion ahead of the passed vehicle.
choiceExplanations: The manual says this is not a good idea, since it may encourage the next rider to cut back in too early.
Slowing immediately closes the gap the next rider needs to complete their own pass.
Stopping on the shoulder is nowhere part of the group passing procedure.

questions.question: How should a group enter a freeway or interstate?
choices: In single file, forming up only after all riders have safely merged
In staggered formation from the start of the ramp
Two abreast, to take up less road
In whatever order riders arrive at the ramp
questions.explanation: The manual says a staggered formation is essential when riding on freeways and interstates, but to enter in single file and form up only after all riders have safely merged in traffic. It adds that the lead rider should move the group over at least one lane to keep entering and exiting vehicles from disrupting the formation.
choiceExplanations: The staggered formation is essential on the freeway itself, but it is formed after merging.
Riding two abreast in a lane is against the manual's rules everywhere.
The manual gives a specific procedure rather than leaving entry to chance.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the manual's ten rules of group riding?
choices: Close up to less than one second in heavy traffic to keep the group together
Base the length of the route and segments on the ability of the least experienced rider
Do not pass within the group, except in the case of emergency
Check your mirrors frequently to ensure the group stays together
questions.explanation: The manual says the opposite: in heavy traffic, resist the temptation to ride too close together, and maintain your minimum one-second, two-second staggered formation space cushion. Keeping adequate following distance is itself one of the ten rules.
choiceExplanations: This is one of the ten rules, and it also governs the pace through curves.
This is one of the ten rules exactly as written.
This is one of the ten rules exactly as written.

questions.question: A rider in your group insists on riding faster than everyone else. What does the manual suggest?
choices: Allow them to go ahead to an agreed meeting point
Move them to the sweep position to slow them down
Increase the group's pace to match them
Have the leader block them from passing
questions.explanation: The manual says that if a rider insists on riding faster than the group, allow him or her to go ahead to an agreed meeting point. That keeps the group's pace tied to the least experienced rider rather than the fastest.
choiceExplanations: The sweep rider sets the pace and should be one of the most experienced, not the fastest.
Raising the whole group's pace pushes the least experienced rider beyond their ability.
Blocking creates exactly the competition the group rules are written to prevent.

questions.question: What share of fatally injured motorcycle riders had BAC levels above the legal limit?
choices: Nearly a third
About one in ten
About two-thirds
Fewer than one in twenty
questions.explanation: The manual reports that studies show nearly a third of all fatally injured motorcycle riders had BAC levels above the legal limit of 0.08%. It adds that a further 8% had lower alcohol levels of 0.01 to 0.07%, showing that a drink or two is enough to impair riding skills.
choiceExplanations: One in ten badly understates the figure the manual reports.
Two-thirds overstates it; the manual's figure is nearly a third.
The manual's figure is far higher than one in twenty.

questions.question: In crashes involving abuse of substances, injuries occur in what share of motorcycle crashes?
questions.explanation: The manual states that injuries occur in 90% of motorcycle crashes and 33% of automobile crashes that involve abuse of substances. The same impairment produces far worse outcomes on a motorcycle, because there is no structure between the rider and the road.
choiceExplanations: Thirty-three percent is the figure the manual gives for automobile crashes, not motorcycle crashes.
Fifty percent is not a figure the manual uses here.
Ten percent is far below the manual's figure.

questions.question: Why does alcohol affect a rider so quickly?
choices: Unlike most foods and beverages, it does not need to be digested
It is absorbed through the skin as well as the stomach
It is heavier than blood and reaches the brain first
It raises body temperature, speeding circulation
questions.explanation: The manual says alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly because, unlike most foods and beverages, it does not need to be digested. Within minutes after being consumed it reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
choiceExplanations: The manual describes absorption into the bloodstream, not through the skin.
Density is not the mechanism the manual describes.
No temperature-based mechanism appears in the manual.

source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly. Unlike most foods and beverages, it does not need to be digested.

questions.question: What is the major effect alcohol has on the body?
choices: It slows down and impairs bodily functions, both mental and physical
It affects physical coordination but not judgment
It affects judgment but not physical coordination
It affects only night vision
questions.explanation: The manual says the major effect alcohol has is to slow down and impair bodily functions — both mental and physical — and that whatever activity you do, you do less well after consuming alcohol.
choiceExplanations: Judgment is affected first, so the mental half cannot be excluded.
Physical tasks are performed less skilfully too, so both halves are affected.
The manual describes a general impairment, not a narrow visual one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: The major effect alcohol has is to slow down and impair bodily functions - both mental and physical.

questions.question: What does BAC stand for and measure?
choices: Blood Alcohol Concentration — the amount of alcohol in relation to blood in the body
Breath Alcohol Count — the number of drinks detected on the breath
Body Alcohol Capacity — how much alcohol a person can tolerate
Blood Alcohol Clearance — how fast alcohol leaves the body
questions.explanation: The manual defines Blood Alcohol Concentration, or BAC, as the amount of alcohol in relation to blood in the body, and states that the more alcohol in your blood, the greater the degree of impairment.
choiceExplanations: BAC is a concentration in the blood, not a count of drinks on the breath.
Tolerance is not what BAC measures; concentration is.
Clearance describes elimination rate, which is a separate concept.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Blood Alcohol Concentration or BAC is the amount of alcohol in relation to blood in the body.

questions.question: Which three primary factors determine BAC?
choices: How much you drink, how fast you drink, and your body weight
How much you drink, what you eat, and your age
The type of alcohol, the time of day, and your height
Your tolerance, your experience, and the temperature
questions.explanation: The manual names three primary factors that play a major part in determining BAC: the amount of alcohol you consume, how fast you drink, and your body weight. It adds that other factors such as sex, physical condition and food intake may push BAC even higher.
choiceExplanations: Food intake and other factors contribute, but the three primary ones include drinking speed and weight.
Type of drink does not matter — the standard drinks all contain the same alcohol.
Tolerance is not one of the primary factors the manual names.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Three primary factors play a major part in determining BAC:

questions.question: Which of these contains the same amount of alcohol as a 12-ounce can of beer?
choices: A 5-ounce glass of wine
A 12-ounce glass of wine
A 5-ounce shot of hard liquor
A half-pint of hard liquor
questions.explanation: The manual states that a 12-ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with one shot of 1.5 ounces of hard liquor, and a 5-ounce glass of wine all contain the same amount of alcohol. Switching drinks does not reduce what reaches your bloodstream.
choiceExplanations: Twelve ounces of wine is more than twice the standard 5-ounce serving.
The standard shot is 1.5 ounces, not 5 ounces.
A half-pint is eight ounces of spirits, far more than one standard drink.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: A 12-ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with one shot (1.5 ounces) of hard liquor, and a 5-ounce glass of wine all contain the same amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A rider says they only had beer, not spirits, so they are fine to ride. What does the manual say?
choices: A beer, a 1.5-ounce shot and a 5-ounce glass of wine all contain the same amount of alcohol
Beer clears the system faster than spirits
Beer affects judgment less than spirits
Beer is safe below three cans in an evening
questions.explanation: The manual's drink-equivalence point exists precisely to answer this. A 12-ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with one 1.5-ounce shot of hard liquor, and a 5-ounce glass of wine all contain the same amount of alcohol, so counting drinks by type tells you nothing useful.
choiceExplanations: Elimination runs at almost one drink per hour regardless of what the drink was.
The manual draws no distinction between drink types in their effect on judgment.
No safe quantity of any drink is offered anywhere in the manual.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: A 12-ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with one shot (1.5 ounces) of hard liquor, and a 5-ounce glass of wine all contain the same amount of alcohol.

questions.question: At roughly what rate does the body eliminate alcohol?
choices: Almost one drink per hour
About two drinks per hour
About one drink every three hours
It varies entirely with body weight
questions.explanation: The manual says that generally, alcohol can be eliminated in the body at the rate of almost one drink per hour. That single figure is what makes the arithmetic of waiting possible — and what shows that drinking faster than one an hour accumulates alcohol.
choiceExplanations: Two drinks per hour is faster than the body can clear, which is why drinks accumulate.
One drink every three hours is slower than the rate the manual gives.
Body weight affects BAC, but the manual gives a general elimination rate of almost one drink per hour.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: alcohol can be eliminated in the body at the rate of almost one drink per hour

questions.question: You drink four drinks over two hours. How many remain in your system at the end?
choices: At least two
None, if you have eaten
At least three
One at most
questions.explanation: This is the manual's own worked example: four drinks over the span of two hours leaves at least two (4 − 2 = 2) drinks remaining in your system at the end of the two hours, and you would need at least another two hours to eliminate them before you consider riding.
choiceExplanations: Food intake may affect BAC, but it does not eliminate alcohol that is already in the bloodstream.
Two hours of elimination removes about two drinks, leaving two rather than three.
Four drinks minus about two hours of elimination leaves two, not one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: If you drink two drinks in an hour, at the end of that hour, at least one drink will remain in your bloodstream.

questions.question: You drink seven drinks over three hours. How much longer does the manual say you must wait before considering riding?
choices: At least another four hours
At least another two hours
At least another seven hours
No additional time — three hours is enough
questions.explanation: The manual works this example through: seven drinks over three hours leaves at least four (7 − 3 = 4) drinks in your system, and you would need at least another four hours to eliminate the alcohol from those four remaining drinks before you consider riding.
choiceExplanations: Two hours would only clear about two of the four drinks still in your system.
Seven hours is the time for all seven drinks, ignoring the three already elapsed.
Three hours clears about three drinks, leaving four still in your system.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: The faster you drink, the more alcohol accumulates in your body.

questions.question: In all but one state, an adult is considered intoxicated at what BAC?
choices: 0.08% or above
0.05% or above
0.10% or above
0.02% or above
questions.explanation: The manual states that in all but one state, an adult with a BAC of 0.08% or above is considered intoxicated, noting that in Utah the threshold is 0.05%.
choiceExplanations: 0.05% is the threshold in the one state the manual names as an exception, Utah.
0.10% is above the standard adult limit the manual states.
0.02% relates to the lower limits that apply to operators under 21.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: In all but one state, an adult with a BAC of 0.08% or above is considered intoxicated (in Utah the threshold is 0.05%).

questions.question: What BAC limits apply to operators under the age of 21?
choices: Lower limits of 0.00 to 0.02%, depending on the state
The same 0.08% limit as adults
0.05% in every state
There is no separate limit for riders under 21
questions.explanation: The manual says that for operators under the age of 21, lower BAC limits of 0.00 to 0.02%, depending on state, apply. In practice that means any measurable alcohol can put a young rider over the limit.
choiceExplanations: The adult limit does not apply; under-21 operators face a stricter standard.
The manual gives a range of 0.00 to 0.02%, which varies by state, not a single 0.05% figure.
The manual states plainly that lower limits apply to operators under 21.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: For operators under the age of 21, lower BAC limits (0.00 to 0.02%, depending on state) apply.

questions.question: What does the manual say about impairment relative to the legal limit?
choices: Impairment of judgment and skills begins well below the legal limit
Impairment begins only once the legal limit is exceeded
Impairment is unpredictable and cannot be described
Impairment begins at about half the legal limit and not before
questions.explanation: The manual says whether or not you are legally intoxicated is not the real issue, because impairment of judgment and skills begins well below the legal limit. Judgment and decision-making are affected long before legal limits are reached.
choiceExplanations: The manual says the legal threshold is not the point at which impairment starts.
The manual describes the pattern of impairment clearly, beginning with judgment.
No half-the-limit threshold appears; impairment begins well below the limit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Impairment of judgment and skills begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: Which ability does alcohol affect first?
choices: Your ability to judge how well you are riding
Your grip strength
Your night vision
Your reaction time
questions.explanation: The manual says your ability to judge how well you are riding is affected first: although you may be performing more and more poorly, you think you are doing better and better, so you ride confidently and take greater and greater risks.
choiceExplanations: Physical strength is not what the manual identifies as the first casualty.
Vision is affected, but the manual names self-assessment as the first thing to go.
Reaction time degrades, but judgment of your own performance is affected first.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Your ability to judge how well you are riding is affected first.

questions.question: A rider has had two drinks, feels sharper than usual, and says their riding is fine. What does the manual say about that feeling?
choices: It is the expected effect — judgment of your own riding is impaired first
It is accurate if they have waited an hour per drink
It is a sign their tolerance is high enough to ride safely
It only applies to riders who drink regularly
questions.explanation: The manual describes exactly this trap: your ability to judge how well you are riding is affected first, so although you may be performing more and more poorly, you think you are doing better and better. The confidence is a symptom, not evidence.
choiceExplanations: Waiting one hour per drink still leaves side effects, and self-assessment remains unreliable.
The manual says no one is immune to the effects of alcohol; tolerance is not protection.
The manual makes no exception for occasional drinkers.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Your ability to judge how well you are riding is affected first.

questions.question: What does the manual say about setting a limit or pacing yourself?
choices: They are poor alternatives at best, because judgment is one of the first things affected
They are the recommended approach for social riders
They work provided you eat beforehand
They are sufficient if you stay below the legal limit
questions.explanation: The manual says setting a limit or pacing yourself are poor alternatives at best, because your ability to use good judgment is one of the first things affected by alcohol. Its two real options are 'don't drink' — since once you start, your resistance is weaker — or 'don't ride'.
choiceExplanations: The manual explicitly rejects these as strategies rather than recommending them.
Food may affect BAC but does not restore the judgment needed to hold to a limit.
Impairment begins well below the legal limit, so staying under it is not sufficient.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Setting a limit or pacing yourself are poor alternatives at best.

questions.question: If you have been drinking and cannot ride, what does the manual suggest doing with the motorcycle?
choices: Leave it, so you will not be tempted to ride, and arrange another way home
Ride it slowly on back roads only
Ride it after one hour regardless of how much you drank
Push it home on foot
questions.explanation: The manual's advice under 'Or Don't Ride' is to leave the motorcycle so you won't be tempted to ride and arrange another way to get home, and to wait until your system eliminates the alcohol and its fatiguing after-effects if you have exceeded your limit.
choiceExplanations: Reduced speed does not restore judgment or skill, and back roads are still public roads.
The elimination rate is about one drink per hour, so a single hour rarely suffices.
The manual does not suggest this; it suggests leaving the motorcycle and arranging a lift.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Leave the motorcycle - so you won't be tempted to ride.

questions.question: Why does the manual say it falls to others to stop a friend riding after drinking?
choices: People who have had too much to drink are unable to make a responsible decision
Friends are legally liable for letting them ride
The rider's insurance requires a second opinion
A drinking rider will always ask for help
questions.explanation: The manual says people who have had too much to drink are unable to make a responsible decision, so it is up to others to step in and keep them from taking too great a risk. It acknowledges this is uncomfortable and rarely thanked for at the time — but the alternatives are often worse.
choiceExplanations: The manual makes a practical argument, not a legal one about liability.
Insurance is mentioned only as a consequence of a DUI conviction.
The manual says intervening is uncomfortable and rarely thanked for, not that help is requested.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.section: Step in to Protect a Friend
source.sourceQuote: People who have had too much to drink are unable to make a responsible decision.

questions.question: Which of these does the manual list as a way to keep a friend from riding impaired?
choices: Take their key, if you can, and secure their bike
Let them ride if they promise to go slowly
Follow them home on your own motorcycle
Give them strong coffee, which removes the impairment
questions.explanation: The manual lists several approaches: arrange a safe ride, slow the pace of drinking by involving them in other activities, keep them there with food and coffee to pass the time, take their key if you can and secure their bike, and get friends involved to apply peer pressure.
choiceExplanations: A promise to ride slowly does nothing about the impaired judgment making the promise.
Escorting an impaired rider does not make them safe to ride.
Coffee is suggested to pass the time, not as something that sobers a person up.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.section: Step in to Protect a Friend
source.sourceQuote: Take their key, if you can, and secure their bike.

questions.question: What does the manual say cannabis does to a rider's perception?
choices: It distorts perception of time, space and speed
It sharpens perception of speed but dulls peripheral vision
It has no measurable effect on perception below a certain dose
It affects only colour vision
questions.explanation: The manual says that although cannabis may be legal for medicinal or recreational use in your state, it is still not legal, safe, or wise to operate a motor vehicle while impaired by it, since it tends to distort your perception of time, space and speed — the judgments a rider makes constantly.
choiceExplanations: Nothing in the manual describes cannabis as sharpening any perception.
The manual offers no safe dose; it says do not operate a vehicle while impaired by cannabis.
Colour vision is not what the manual identifies as affected.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: it tends to distort your perception of time, space and speed

questions.question: How long do the effects of smoked cannabis generally last, according to the manual?
choices: From 2 to 4 hours
About 30 minutes
More than 6 hours
About 12 hours
questions.explanation: The manual says that when cannabis is smoked, its effects generally begin within a few minutes and can last from 2 to 4 hours. Eaten cannabis is different: onset could be delayed more than an hour and the duration could be more than 6 hours.
choiceExplanations: Thirty minutes is far shorter than the manual's stated duration.
More than 6 hours is the duration the manual gives for eaten cannabis, not smoked.
Twelve hours is not a figure the manual uses.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: When cannabis is smoked, its effects generally begin within a few minutes and can last from 2 to 4 hours.

questions.question: How does eaten cannabis differ from smoked cannabis?
choices: Onset may be delayed more than an hour and the effects can last more than 6 hours
It produces no impairment of riding ability
It takes effect faster but wears off sooner
It is exempt from riding-under-the-influence laws
questions.explanation: The manual contrasts the two: smoked cannabis takes effect within a few minutes and lasts 2 to 4 hours, but when cannabis is eaten the onset of effects could be delayed for more than an hour and the duration of the high could be more than 6 hours. It adds that riders impaired by cannabis can be convicted of riding under the influence and face similar harsh penalties.
choiceExplanations: The manual treats cannabis impairment as real regardless of how it is consumed.
The manual says the opposite: onset is delayed and the effects last longer.
Riders impaired by cannabis can be convicted of riding under the influence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
