questions.question: How does riding a motorcycle compare with driving a car for fatigue?
choices: Riding is more tiring, so you will tire sooner on a long trip
Riding is less tiring because of the fresh air
They are equally tiring
Riding is only more tiring above 60 mph
questions.explanation: The manual says riding a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car, and that on a long trip you will tire sooner than you would in a car. Its instruction is to avoid riding when tired, because fatigue can affect your control of the motorcycle.
choiceExplanations: Wind, cold and rain make you tire more quickly, not less.
The manual states clearly that riding is more tiring than driving.
No speed threshold is attached to the fatigue comparison.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Riding a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car.

questions.question: How often does the manual say to stop and get off the motorcycle on a long ride?
choices: At least every two hours
At least every four hours
At least every six hours
Only when you feel tired
questions.explanation: The manual says to take frequent rest breaks: stop and get off the motorcycle at least every two hours. It also notes that experienced riders seldom try to ride more than about six hours a day.
choiceExplanations: Four hours is longer than the manual's stated interval for rest breaks.
Six hours is the limit experienced riders place on a whole day's riding, not on a break interval.
Waiting for fatigue to arrive is the opposite of the manual's preventive advice.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Stop and get off the motorcycle at least every two hours.

questions.question: What does the manual say about using stimulants to stay alert on a long ride?
choices: Artificial stimulants often result in extreme fatigue or depression when they wear off
They are acceptable if used only in the final hour of a ride
They restore judgment impaired by alcohol
They are recommended for night riding
questions.explanation: The manual's advice is 'don't drink or use drugs', because artificial stimulants often result in extreme fatigue or depression when they wear off, leaving riders unable to concentrate on the task at hand. Its fatigue remedies are protection from the elements, limited distance and frequent breaks.
choiceExplanations: The manual gives no safe window for stimulant use on a ride.
Nothing reverses alcohol impairment except time.
The manual advises against stimulants rather than recommending them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Artificial stimulants often result in extreme fatigue or depression when they wear off.

questions.question: Which of these does the manual NOT give as a way to manage fatigue?
choices: Drinking coffee at each stop to extend your riding day
Protecting yourself from wind, cold and rain
Limiting your distance — experienced riders seldom ride more than about six hours a day
Taking frequent rest breaks
questions.explanation: The manual's fatigue list is: protect yourself from the elements, limit your distance, take frequent rest breaks, and don't drink or use drugs. Coffee appears only as something to serve a friend who should not be riding, never as a way to extend a riding day.
choiceExplanations: This is on the list — wind, cold and rain make you tire quickly, so dress warmly.
This is on the list exactly as written.
This is on the list — stop and get off the motorcycle at least every two hours.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Wind, cold, and rain make you tire quickly.

questions.question: What does the manual say about combining alcohol with other drugs?
choices: The combined effects are more dangerous than either is alone
The effects cancel each other out
Prescription drugs are exempt from this concern
Only illegal drugs interact with alcohol
questions.explanation: The manual says many over-the-counter, prescription and illegal drugs have side effects that increase the risk of riding, and that we know the combined effects of alcohol and drugs are more dangerous than either is alone. It also states that no one is immune to the effects of alcohol or drugs.
choiceExplanations: Nothing in the manual suggests impairments offset one another.
The manual names over-the-counter and prescription drugs alongside illegal ones.
Many over-the-counter and prescription drugs have side effects that increase the risk of riding.

questions.question: A parked van on your right hides you from a driver waiting on the cross street ahead. Where should you position yourself?
choices: In the left portion of the lane, away from the van, so the driver sees you sooner
In the right portion of the lane, close to the van, to shorten your path
In the centre of the lane, so both sides are equal
Behind the van, so you are shielded until the junction
questions.explanation: This is the manual's own illustration of a blind intersection: the rider has moved to the left portion of the lane — away from the parked car — so the driver on the cross street can see him earlier. The rule is to move to the portion of the lane that brings you into the other driver's field of vision at the earliest possible moment.
choiceExplanations: Riding close to the van keeps you hidden behind it for as long as possible.
The centre is the answer when hazards sit on both sides, not when the sight line is blocked on one.
Using the van as a shield means the waiting driver never sees you until you appear at the junction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Intersections and Conspicuity
source.sourceQuote: If you approach a blind intersection, move to the portion of the lane that will bring you into another driver's field of vision at the earliest possible moment.

questions.question: Which statement about parking a motorcycle at a curb is NOT correct?
choices: Every city requires motorcycles to park at an angle to the curb
In a parallel space, position the motorcycle at an angle with the rear wheel to the curb
Some cities have ordinances requiring motorcycles to park parallel to the curb
Loose and sloped shoulders can make setting the side or centre stand difficult
questions.explanation: The manual gives the angled, rear-wheel-to-the-curb position as its method, but immediately notes that some cities have ordinances that require motorcycles to park parallel to the curb. So the one thing you cannot say is that every city requires the angled position.
choiceExplanations: This is correct — it is the manual's stated method for a parallel parking space.
This is correct — the manual notes this local variation explicitly.
This is correct, and it appears in the manual's advice on getting off the road.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Intersections and Conspicuity
source.sourceQuote: If parking in a parallel parking space next to a curb, position the motorcycle at an angle with the rear wheel to the curb.

questions.question: The manual says it is not always possible to stop quickly enough to avoid an obstacle. What must a rider therefore also be able to do?
choices: Swerve around the obstacle
Lock the rear wheel deliberately
Accelerate past the obstacle
Lay the motorcycle down
questions.explanation: The manual says it is not always desirable or possible to stop quickly to avoid an obstacle, so riders must also be able to swerve around one — and that determining which skill the situation needs is important as well. Stopping and swerving are the two crash-avoidance skills it names.
choiceExplanations: Locking the rear wheel removes your ability to change direction, which is the opposite of what is needed.
Accelerating toward an obstacle does not avoid it and shortens your remaining options.
Deliberately dropping the motorcycle is nowhere described in the manual as a technique.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Know when and how to stop or swerve, two skills critical in avoiding a crash.

questions.question: A pothole lies directly in your path with a clear lane to the left. What is the manual's first preference?
choices: Avoid it by slowing or going around it
Ride over it at a 90 degree angle
Ride over it while accelerating hard
Brake hard on top of it to reduce the impact
questions.explanation: The manual's order of preference is explicit: try to avoid obstacles by slowing or going around them. Only if you must go over a smaller obstacle do you approach it at as close to a 90 degree angle as possible and use the rise-off-the-seat technique.
choiceExplanations: Crossing at 90 degrees is the technique for when you must go over an obstacle, not the first choice.
Hard acceleration over a pothole is not a technique the manual teaches.
Braking on the obstacle loads the front wheel at exactly the wrong moment.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If you must go over a smaller obstacle, approach it at as close to a 90˚ angle as possible.

questions.question: Railroad tracks cross the road at a shallow diagonal. You are in the right-hand lane with traffic in the left lane. What does the manual advise?
choices: Ride straight within your lane to cross them
Move into the left lane to square the tracks up to 90 degrees
Stop before the tracks and cross at walking pace
Cross at exactly 45 degrees regardless of lane position
questions.explanation: The manual says it is usually safer to ride straight within your lane to cross tracks, and warns that turning to take tracks at a 90 degree angle can be more dangerous because the direction may put you into another lane of traffic. Traffic alongside makes that warning concrete.
choiceExplanations: Turning to take tracks at 90 degrees can put you into another lane of traffic, which is the greater risk.
Nothing in the manual requires stopping at a crossing, and it does not solve the angle problem.
Forty-five degrees is the rule for seams running parallel to your path, not for a crossing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.section: Railroad Tracks, Trolley Tracks and Pavement Seams
source.sourceQuote: Usually it is safer to ride straight within your lane to cross tracks.

questions.question: The back of your motorcycle begins to jerk and sway from side to side. What should you suspect?
choices: A rear tire failure
A locked front brake
An engine seizure
A broken headlight bracket
questions.explanation: The manual says you will seldom hear a tire go flat, so a change in handling is the warning. A front tire going down makes the steering feel heavy; a rear one makes the back of the motorcycle jerk or sway from side to side. Either way, hold the handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle and keep a straight course.
choiceExplanations: A locked front brake causes immediate loss of steering and balance, not a rear-end sway.
Engine seizure announces itself as a loss of power or a change in the engine's sound.
A loose bracket does not produce the handling change the manual describes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If the motorcycle starts handling differently, it may be a tire failure.

questions.question: You feel an instant loss of power to the rear wheel on a motorcycle with a chain drive. What does the manual say to do?
choices: Close the throttle and brake to a stop in a safe area
Downshift to regain drive
Accelerate to clear the traffic behind you
Apply only the rear brake, in case the chain has jammed
questions.explanation: The manual says that if the chain or belt breaks, you'll notice an instant loss of power to the rear wheel — close the throttle and brake to a stop in a safe area. The greater danger is a chain or belt that slips or breaks and locks the rear wheel, causing a skid.
choiceExplanations: With a broken chain there is no drive to regain, whatever gear you select.
A broken drive train means the throttle has no effect on your speed.
The manual gives no instruction to favour one brake after a chain failure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If the chain or belt breaks, you'll notice an instant loss of power to the rear wheel.

questions.question: Why does the manual say to stay in your lane rather than swerve for a small animal in traffic?
choices: Hitting something small is less dangerous to you than hitting something big, like a car
Swerving is illegal within a traffic lane
Small animals usually move out of the way in time
Swerving would damage the tires more than the impact
questions.explanation: The manual tells you to do everything you safely can to avoid hitting an animal, but adds that if you are in traffic you should remain in your lane, because hitting something small is less dangerous to you than hitting something big — like a car.
choiceExplanations: The manual gives a risk comparison, not a legal rule.
The manual makes no assumption about what the animal will do.
Tire damage is not the reasoning behind the instruction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Hitting something small is less dangerous to you than hitting something big - like a car.

questions.question: What does the manual say to do as a first step when a dog is chasing you?
choices: Downshift and approach the animal slowly
Accelerate away immediately
Brake to a complete stop
Swerve into the adjacent lane
questions.explanation: The manual's sequence is two-part: if you are being chased, downshift and approach the animal slowly, and as you approach it, accelerate and leave the animal behind. It also says not to kick at the animal, and to keep control and look where you want to go.
choiceExplanations: Accelerating comes second, as you reach the animal — not as the first response.
Stopping leaves you stationary beside an agitated animal with no way out.
Changing lanes for an animal is exactly what the manual warns against in traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: If you are being chased, downshift and approach the animal slowly.

questions.question: Which of these does the manual list as objects that strike riders?
choices: Insects, cigarettes thrown from cars, and pebbles kicked up by the vehicle ahead
Loose gravel from the shoulder only
Debris from your own motorcycle
Rain and hail only
questions.explanation: The manual says that from time to time riders are struck by insects, cigarettes thrown from cars or pebbles kicked up by the tires of the vehicle ahead. If you are wearing face protection it might get smeared or cracked; without it, an object could hit you in the eye, face or mouth.
choiceExplanations: Road-edge gravel is covered under slippery surfaces, not flying objects.
The manual describes objects coming from other vehicles and the environment, not from your own machine.
Weather is addressed under riding gear and slippery surfaces, not flying objects.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Whatever happens, keep your eyes on the road and your hands on the handlebars.

questions.question: A rider with two months of experience is asked to take a friend on the back. What does the manual's guidance indicate?
choices: They should not — only experienced riders should attempt to carry passengers
They may, provided they stay on quiet roads
They may, provided the passenger is lighter than they are
They may, provided they have completed a pre-ride inspection
questions.explanation: The manual says the extra weight of a passenger or cargo affects the way your motorcycle handles, requiring extra practice, preparation and caution, and for that reason only experienced riders should attempt to carry passengers or large loads. Two months is well inside the under-five-months window the manual links to more than half of all crashes.
choiceExplanations: Road type does not change the handling difference a passenger creates.
Passenger weight changes the degree of the effect, not whether the rider is ready for it.
A pre-ride inspection is necessary but is not what makes a rider experienced.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: only experienced riders should attempt to carry passengers or large loads

questions.question: What does the manual say about two riders travelling side by side in the same lane?
choices: Never do it — wait until you are both stopped to talk
It is acceptable on wide lanes at low speed
It is the preferred formation in heavy traffic
It is acceptable provided both riders signal first
questions.explanation: The manual says never ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane, because there is no place to go if you have to manoeuvre to avoid a car or hazard in the roadway, and to wait until you are both stopped to talk.
choiceExplanations: Lane width is not the issue; the absence of an escape path is, at any speed.
In heavy traffic the manual says to resist riding too close together, not to pair up.
Signalling does not create the escape room that pairing up removes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: Never ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane.

questions.question: You are the fourth rider in a staggered formation. What spacing does the manual give you?
choices: At least two seconds from the second rider, in the right side of the lane
At least one second from the third rider, in the left side of the lane
Directly alongside the third rider
At least four seconds behind the leader, in the centre of the lane
questions.explanation: The manual sets the pattern out rider by rider: the leader on the left, the second at least one second back on the right, the third in the left position at least two seconds behind the first rider, and the fourth keeping at least a two-second distance from the second rider on the right side of the lane.
choiceExplanations: The one-second spacing is the second rider's gap behind the leader, and the fourth rides on the right.
Riding alongside another rider in the same lane is forbidden.
The formation alternates left and right sides; nobody holds the centre, and there is no four-second rule.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: The third maintains the left position of the lane, at least two seconds behind the first rider.

questions.question: The manual notes that a further 8% of fatally injured riders had BAC levels of 0.01 to 0.07%. What does it say this demonstrates?
choices: That having only a drink or two in one's system is enough to impair riding skills
That low BAC levels are harmless in practice
That most impaired riders are well over the limit
That BAC testing is unreliable at low levels
questions.explanation: The manual reports that nearly a third of fatally injured riders were over 0.08%, and adds that an additional 8% had lower alcohol levels of 0.01 to 0.07%, demonstrating that having only a drink or two in one's system is enough to impair riding skills.
choiceExplanations: The manual cites the figure to show the opposite — that low levels still impair.
The point of citing the lower band is that impairment is not confined to those over the limit.
Nothing in the manual questions the reliability of BAC testing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Studies show that nearly a third of all fatally injured motorcycle riders had BAC levels above the legal limit of 0.08%.

questions.question: Which comparison does the manual make between motorcyclists and drivers where substance abuse is involved?
choices: Injuries occur in 90% of motorcycle crashes but 33% of automobile crashes
Drinking is a bigger problem among motorcyclists than among drivers
Motorcyclists are less likely to be tested after a crash
Motorcyclists recover faster because the impacts are lighter
questions.explanation: The manual says drinking and drug use is as big a problem among motorcyclists as it is among automobile drivers, but motorcyclists are more likely to be killed or severely injured: injuries occur in 90% of motorcycle crashes and 33% of automobile crashes that involve abuse of substances.
choiceExplanations: The manual says drinking and drug use is as big a problem among motorcyclists as among drivers, not bigger.
Testing rates are not a comparison the manual draws.
Motorcyclists are more likely to be killed or severely injured, not less.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Injuries occur in 90% of motorcycle crashes and 33% of automobile crashes that involve abuse of substances.

questions.question: Which statement describes the relationship between BAC and impairment?
choices: The more alcohol in your blood, the greater the degree of impairment
Impairment is fixed once any alcohol is present, regardless of amount
Impairment depends only on how recently you drank, not how much
Impairment falls once BAC passes its peak, even while alcohol remains
questions.explanation: The manual defines BAC as the amount of alcohol in relation to blood in the body, and states that the more alcohol in your blood, the greater the degree of impairment. It also warns that alcohol may accumulate even when drinking at one drink per hour.
choiceExplanations: The manual describes impairment as proportional to concentration, not as a fixed switch.
Timing affects BAC, but the manual ties the degree of impairment to the concentration itself.
Alcohol still in the body is still impairing; nothing in the manual describes a recovery at peak.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Blood Alcohol Concentration or BAC is the amount of alcohol in relation to blood in the body.

questions.question: Two riders of different body weights drink the same amount over the same time. What does the manual's account of BAC predict?
choices: Their BAC levels will differ, because body weight is one of the three primary factors
Their BAC levels will be identical, since the amount and time match
Body weight only matters above four drinks
The heavier rider will reach a higher BAC
questions.explanation: The manual names three primary factors in determining BAC: the amount of alcohol you consume, how fast you drink, and your body weight. Matching two of the three does not produce the same BAC, and other factors such as sex, physical condition and food intake can raise it further still.
choiceExplanations: Body weight is explicitly one of the three primary factors, so matching the other two is not enough.
No threshold makes body weight start to matter; it is a primary factor throughout.
The manual names weight as a factor without suggesting extra weight raises BAC.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Three primary factors play a major part in determining BAC:

questions.question: A rider's BAC tests at 0.05%, under the adult legal limit. What does the manual say about their fitness to ride?
choices: They may still be impaired — judgment and skills begin to suffer well below the legal limit
They are unimpaired, since they are below the limit
They are impaired only if they are under 21
They are fine to ride provided they have eaten
questions.explanation: The manual separates the two questions: whether or not you are legally intoxicated is not the real issue, because impairment of judgment and skills begins well below the legal limit. Judgment and decision-making are affected long before legal limits are reached.
choiceExplanations: Being under the limit answers a legal question, not the question of whether skill is impaired.
Under-21 riders face stricter limits, but impairment below the limit applies to everyone.
Food may affect BAC but does not restore impaired judgment and skill.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: Impairment of judgment and skills begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: An 18-year-old rider has a BAC of 0.03%. How does the manual describe the legal position?
choices: Lower limits of 0.00 to 0.02% apply to operators under 21, depending on the state
The adult limit of 0.08% applies until they turn 21
There is no legal limit below 21, only a rider-education requirement
The limit is 0.05% for every rider under 21
questions.explanation: The manual states that for operators under the age of 21, lower BAC limits of 0.00 to 0.02%, depending on state, apply. A reading of 0.03% is above the top of that range, so the adult limit is the wrong yardstick here.
choiceExplanations: The adult 0.08% figure does not apply to operators under the age of 21.
The manual states plainly that lower BAC limits apply to under-21 operators.
0.05% is the adult threshold in the one exception state, not the under-21 limit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Being in Shape to Ride
source.sourceQuote: For operators under the age of 21, lower BAC limits (0.00 to 0.02%, depending on state) apply.

questions.question: You are choosing a jacket for daytime commuting in traffic. What does the manual's guidance point to?
choices: A bright orange, red, yellow or green jacket, because most crashes occur in daylight
A black jacket, because it hides road grime
A reflective jacket only, since bright colour adds nothing by day
Any colour, since colour choice only matters at night
questions.explanation: The manual says most crashes occur during daylight hours, so wear bright-coloured clothing to increase your chances of being seen, and names bright orange, red, yellow or green jackets and vests as your best bets. Your body is half the visible surface area of the rider and motorcycle together.
choiceExplanations: Dark colours are what the manual calls drab, and any bright colour is better.
Reflective material helps at night, but bright colour is the daylight measure and adds to it.
The manual ties bright clothing to daylight specifically, because that is when most crashes occur.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Intersections and Conspicuity
source.sourceQuote: Most crashes occur during daylight hours. Wear bright-colored clothing to increase your chances of being seen.

questions.question: It is a clear, sunny afternoon. What does the manual say about running your headlight?
choices: Keep it on — during the day a motorcycle with its light on is twice as likely to be noticed
Switch it off to avoid dazzling oncoming drivers
Switch it off to save the battery for night riding
Use the high beam, since daylight washes out a low beam
questions.explanation: The manual says a good way to help others see your motorcycle is to have the headlight on at all times, and gives the figure: during the day, a motorcycle with its light on is twice as likely to be noticed. Daylight is when most crashes happen, which is exactly when that doubling matters.
choiceExplanations: The manual never suggests switching the headlight off; it says to keep it on at all times.
Battery conservation is nowhere raised as a reason to run without lights.
High beam is for when you are not following or meeting a car, not a daylight instruction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Intersections and Conspicuity
source.sourceQuote: during the day, a motorcycle with its light on is twice as likely to be noticed

questions.question: A rider habitually stops using mostly the rear brake with a light touch at the front. Which studied error does that match?
choices: Underbraking the front tire and overbraking the rear
Failing to separate braking from swerving
Overriding the headlight
Running wide in a curve
questions.explanation: The manual reports that studies show most crash-involved riders underbrake the front tire and overbrake the rear. Since the front brake provides 70% or more of total stopping power, that habit throws away most of the braking available and risks locking the rear.
choiceExplanations: That error concerns doing both skills at once, not how brake pressure is distributed.
Overriding the headlight is a night-riding error about speed and beam distance.
Running wide in a curve is a cornering error, not a braking distribution problem.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: Underbrake the front tire and overbrake the rear.

questions.question: Which description matches a wobble rather than another problem?
choices: The front wheel and handlebars suddenly shake from side to side
The rear of the motorcycle jerks and sways after a change in handling
The motorcycle weaves gently while crossing a bridge grating
The engine loses power and its note changes
questions.explanation: The manual defines a wobble as occurring when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly start to shake from side to side at any speed, and traces most wobbles to improper loading, unsuitable accessories or incorrect tire pressure.
choiceExplanations: That describes a rear tire failure, which is dealt with by easing off the throttle and holding a straight course.
That is the weave caused by rain grooves or gratings, which the manual says is generally not hazardous.
That is the first sign of engine seizure, usually caused by low oil.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Crash Avoidance and Hazards
source.sourceQuote: A “wobble” occurs when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly start to shake from side to side at any speed.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT something the manual requires before carrying a passenger?
choices: A windscreen to shelter the passenger from windblast
Passenger footrests
A seat large enough to hold both of you without crowding
A strap or solid handholds for the passenger
questions.explanation: The manual's passenger equipment list is footrests, a proper seat large enough for both of you without crowding, and a strap or solid handholds. A windshield is discussed as rider comfort on long rides and as no substitute for eye protection, but it is not passenger equipment.
choiceExplanations: This is required — the manual names passenger footrests explicitly.
This is required — the manual says you should not have to sit more forward than usual.
This is required — the passenger needs something secure to hold onto.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Motorcycle Operator Manual, 18th edition (Motorcycle Safety Foundation), retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 3153bb43aa19c5037198e63dab8b764f2c4042118e1e0b3cae4f1c263ba7148c
source.chapterTitle: Ride Within Your Abilities - Passengers, Cargo and Group Riding
source.sourceQuote: Check that there is a strap or solid handholds for your passenger to hold onto.
